chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after li'an, claiming the child was indeed his. I asked: Will the child be returned to him (as a son)? He said: No, and not even with honor, and he will not be returned to him, nor will it be permissible for him until the Day of Resurrection. So he does not contradict the first report, because the meaning of His words 'he will not be returned to him' is that he is not attached to him with complete attachment, so inheritance is established between them. Rather, he is attached to him in that the son inherits from him, but the father does not inherit from the son. And the report that indicates this is the one we presented earlier in the first chapter on Li'an from Zurara, which adds further clarification to that.
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a father who claims his child after performing li'an?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a husband who performs li'an and later retracts his denial to claim paternity does not achieve full legal reinstatement of the son. The Imam explains that the link is partial: the son inherits from the father, but the father does not inherit from the son, a ruling supported by earlier hadiths from Zurara. This distinction highlights the permanence of the li'an bond's specific legal constraints even after retraction.
